Second read (read-only, not built) of head 0d7263ac4e94bcc68cf643ecc5a9280b0af260fd.

**Verdict: no blocker.** The change makes the start angle of a leaning five-axis section known. The guard stays. I found no silent change for streams that do not lean. Three notes follow. Each note is about behaviour that this PR does not add.

### 1. The `A0. B0.` block

- `assets/posts/fanuc.cps:926-933` (`onRapid`): `tilt()` (line 324) arms `G43.4 H01` first. Then `xyFirst` (line 909) writes `G00 Z<clearance>` at the current X/Y. The opening rapid is at the clearance, so the next block is the X/Y traverse with `A0. B0.`. The approach comes after it. The order is: TCP on, Z retract, X/Y and rotation at the clearance, approach. This order is correct.
- The statement "A0 B0" is true at that block: the block commands it. The control then holds it, and `heldAngles` (line 960) writes it to `rotAt`.
- What the code guarantees: the rotation is in a rapid at the section clearance, after the Z retract, before the first feed.
- What the code assumes: the tool body is clear of the part and the stock during the turn from the angle that the last program left. Under `G43.4` the tip stays on the X/Y line only if the control interpolates G00 linearly under TCP. In a non-linear rapid, the tip of a head that turns back to upright can go below its end height. The size is about the pivot length times `(1 - cos)` of half the turn. A prior tilt above 90 degrees (the travel of `tilthead.mch` is ±120) can also put the head body below the tip.
- Shipped machines: `tilthead.mch` is the only machine with two rotaries (head-head, A about X, B about Y). No table-table or head-table machine with two rotaries ships. The one-rotary tables (`doosan-dnm.mch`, `tormach-770mx-microarc4.mch`, `millturn.mch`) turn the work. For those, `first_traverse_posed` (#3084) reads the work through a full turn, so a turn during the traverse is in its envelope. `tormach.cps` already indexes `G0 A0` alone after `G53 G0 Z` at the first motion of each section.
- Compared to main, this is safer: on main, the first `G01` toward the part turned from the unknown angle.
- Recommendation (follow-up, not for this PR): index the rotaries alone at the tool-change height (as `tormach.cps` does) before the X/Y traverse. The decision file drops this option with the reason "new script logic in each dialect". That reason is valid for this fix, but I recommend that it gets a tracked issue.

### 2. "Upright" is the literal zero

- `crates/post/src/post/mod.rs:539-541` writes `[0.0, 0.0, 0.0]`. No kinematics solver maps the upright axis to machine angles. The letters are the canonical pose law of `cl` (A about X, B about Y), as for the existing return-to-upright arm.
- This is true for each shipped machine: on `tilthead.mch` the zero of A and B is the Z column, and 0 is inside the travel. No shipped machine has a non-zero home (no nutating head, no B home at 90).
- The PR does not make this assumption wider than the existing arm after a lean. A future machine with a non-zero upright pose needs a mapping for the two arms.
- Shortest way: the A and B axes of `tilthead.mch` are linear rotaries with limits (±120), so an absolute A0 B0 has one path.

### 3. Streams that do not lean, and 3+2 streams

- Stamp: `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/stamp.rs:222` fills `None` poses only when `leaned` is true. After the first lean, no pose is `None` (lines 208-212). So the fill changes only the stations before the first lean.
- Dump: `leans` (`mod.rs:435`) is computed for each call of `dump`, and `dump` writes one section. So the decision is for each operation, not for each program. A program with one upright operation and one leaning operation gets the zero only in the leaning section.
- The new arm fires only on a move that states the Z column. A 3+2 stream that states its tilt on each move has no Z-column move, so the arm does not fire. Moves with `rotary` (C axis) are not in `leans`.
- At a tool change and at a section end, `fanuc.cps` resets `tcpmOn` and `lastA/B/C` (lines 684, 833). The next leaning section arms `G43.4` again and writes all words, so no stale state is used. `commanded` starts at false in each `dump`, so the zero block occurs again in each leaning section.
- The test `an_upright_stream_that_never_leans_commands_no_angles` pins byte identity for a stream that states only the Z column. The author reports no golden change.

### 4. The guard

- `rotaryFeed` is not changed. The two hand-built streams (prismatic opening, feed first) still refuse by name.
- The stamp states the upright pose only for its own stations before the first lean. The dump commands that pose. So the post "knows" the angle only after a block that commands it. A tool change, a new section or an M-code does not make an angle known: `rotAt` changes only in `heldAngles`, from words that a block wrote.
- Each leaning section states its own angles on its first posed block.
- Note (pre-existing, not in this diff): a stamped section ends under its last lean (the exit rapids hold the pose, `stamp.rs:210`). A next section that does not lean states no angles. I did not find a test that pins the post for an upright section after a leaning one. Please check if an issue tracks this.

### 5. Other posts

- `fanuc.cps` and `doosan-dnm.cps` (RTCP path) arm `G43.4` on the new record and write the words of the rotaries that the machine states (`angleWord`).
- `doosan-dnm.cps` without RTCP (one A table): the record writes `A0` on the opening rapid. A leaning stream with a B word refuses at its tilted record, as before.
- `tormach.cps`: `indexFor` already indexes A0 at the first motion of a section, with or without an A word.
- `mach4.cps`: a vertical A/B/C is not tilted; the leaning moves later refuse as simultaneous, as before.
- Three-axis posts (`grbl`, `grblhal`, `carvera`, `haas`, `mazak`, `sinumerik`, `heidenhain`, `linuxcnc`, `tinyg`): they refuse `has(p.A)` as "tilted move". On a leaning stream they refused before at the tilted record. Now they refuse one record earlier, with the same message. No post prints an angle word that it cannot drive.

### 6. The follow-up #3414

- The approach `G01` that turns A and B while it descends is in the scope of the verifier laws for a pose that changes: law (c3) mid-turn sweep (`crates/sim/src/verify/sweep.rs`, `turn_cells.rs`, `tilt_span.rs`), the mid-move pose for the solid and contact laws (`midpose.rs`), and the fixture sweep (`posed_steel.rs`). These laws start from the pose held coming in. With this PR that pose is commanded (A0 B0), so the verifier start and the machine start agree.
- So the move is checked, not unchecked. #3414 reports that `cam.verify()` passes. P7 is acceptable by the table: no gouge or collision is shown. The issue is a change of approach law ("retract, rotate, approach"), so P8 (design first) is also correct. It is not P1-P3.

### 7. Tests and law

- `stamp_tests::the_stamp_poses_only_moves_that_touch`: `None` changed to "stated and exactly vertical" (`is_vertical`). Same strength, new law.
- `flow::flow5d_states_an_axis_on_every_cut_move`: the loop starts at the first lean. Before, the moves in front of the first lean had no axis and the loop skipped them (`continue`). So no assertion is lost. `n > 20` stays.
- The three post tests and the three app tests pin the claim and the guard.
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in the changed non-test code.
- `crates/post/src/post/mod.rs` is 734 lines at the head (rule: about 400). It was over the limit before; this PR adds 9 lines. A split is owed work.
- The `Changelog:` line is present. `docs/decisions/3300-opening-rotary-pose.md` is present and has chosen, why and dropped. The commit ends with `Fixes #3300`.
